selected_mechanism.name: DPA Title III grid-equipment determination to DOE intent-to-deploy for AEA Beluga-Healy transmission

news_trigger.what_happened: The Alaska Energy Authority's Beluga-Healy Transmission Project combines up to $150 million in DPA funding with $268 million in non-federal funding, representing a planned total investment of $418 million in Alaska's grid. ... Approximately 223 miles of new transmission line connecting Beluga and Healy will be built.

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: Congress appropriated $1B to carry out the Defense Production Act (OBBBA Sec. 30004). A presidential determination under DPA Sec. 303 then declared transmission lines and grid equipment essential to national defense and directed the Secretary of Energy to make purchases and commitments. DOE is now using that authority to announce up to $150M toward an AEA-developed second Southcentral-Interior transmission line, conditioned on $268M in non-federal funding.

layers.name: Appropriation
layers.what_it_does: Provides the money. DOE describes it as $1 billion in federal funding appropriated for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security ($1B figure from DOE page; statute body not fetched).
layers.controlling_actor: Congress (P.L. 119-21, Title III, Banking Committee, Sec. 30004 Appropriations for Defense Production Act); spent by the executive under DPA authority

layers.name: Statutory authority (DPA Sec. 303, 50 USC 4533)
layers.what_it_does: Lets the President make purchases and commitments to build domestic industrial base capability. Under (a)(5) that requires a written, non-delegable presidential determination. Under (a)(7) requirements can be waived in an emergency or to avert a shortfall.

layers.name: Presidential Determination on grid infrastructure (dated 2026-04-20; DOE cites it as No. 2026-10)
layers.what_it_does: Finds grid infrastructure, explicitly including transmission lines and conductors and substations, essential to national defense. Waives section 303(a)(1)-(a)(6). Directs the Secretary of Energy to implement, including making necessary purchases, commitments, and financial instruments.

layers.name: DOE project selection / intent to deploy
layers.what_it_does: DOE announced its intent to deploy DPA funding of up to $150M to Beluga-Healy. It is an intent. No obligation, agreement terms or timeline are published.
layers.controlling_actor: Secretary of Energy (Chris Wright), with the DOE Office of Electricity (Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza)

layers.name: Project developer and non-federal share
layers.what_it_does: AEA, a state public corporation that owns the existing 170-mile Willow-Healy Alaska Intertie, develops the project and must carry the $268M (about 64%) non-federal share. No fetched page names the source of that money.
layers.controlling_actor: Alaska Energy Authority, through its 8-member Board of Directors (next scheduled meeting 2026-11-05)

chokepoint.layer: DOE project selection / intent to deploy
chokepoint.actor: Secretary of Energy, the single officer the April 20, 2026 Presidential Determination authorized and directed to make purchases, commitments, and financial instruments
chokepoint.binary_decision: Whether to turn the announced intent to deploy up to $150M into an obligated DPA Title III agreement with AEA, and on what terms.

selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Railbelt power: up to $150M of the $418M budget is an unobligated DOE intent, so AEA has to line up $268M in non-federal money before the federal piece is real. AEA's board, next meeting Nov 5 2026, is the next public body positioned to act on financing.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: DPA Title III is being used as a grant-like capital vehicle for a state-owned transmission asset. The defense finding is the legal hinge that lets $1B of Banking-committee money skip the normal DOE grant process. That makes it fast but discretionary. Until the Secretary obligates the money the announcement is a signal, not capital. About 64% of the cost sits on the non-federal side, so the real constraint is AEA's ability to finance its share. How costs would be recovered from Railbelt users is not established by any fetched source.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Railbelt utility CFOs and large-load developers should not count on a second Beluga-Healy path being funded or on any delivery timeline until DOE publishes an obligated DPA agreement and AEA identifies the source of the $268M. Before the AEA board's Nov 5 2026 meeting, ask AEA directly for both.
